implementationPlan.description:
DOCS 1 (DoD 1, 2): docs/DEVELOPMENT.md '## Plugin Bundling' only. Edit only from that heading to the `---` before '## Current Feature Coverage'; every other section stays byte-identical. Use the main session's Edit tool: no shell writes, no subagent edits.

READ FIRST (claim nothing beyond these files):
- moe-jetbrains/build.gradle.kts: requireBundledAssets() and the prepareSandbox from/exclude blocks;
- moe-vscode/scripts/bundle-assets.mjs;
- scripts/tests/onboarding.mjs, the `if (bundle)` block;
- scripts/tests/local-runner-bundle.test.mjs;
- .github/workflows/ci.yml (test-typescript, build-plugin, build-all-platforms) and release.yml ('Verify packaged onboarding').

(a) TREE. Replace the stale tree, which lists only moe-agent.ps1/.sh, with what both bundles ship. JetBrains ships `moe-jetbrains/` in the zip, beside `lib/`. VS Code ships `moe-vscode/bundled/`, which becomes `extension/bundled/` in the .vsix.
- lib/: JetBrains only (plugin JARs).
- daemon/ and proxy/: that package's dist minus *.test.* and *.spec.*, its package.json, and node_modules minus .bin.
- scripts/: moe-agent.ps1, plus moe-agent.sh and moe-call.sh (LF-normalized), prompt-cache*.mjs, usage-receipt.mjs, usage-session.mjs, usage-report.mjs, analyze-usage.mjs and moe-account-lease.mjs.
- scripts/local-runner/: everything except *.test.*, *.spec.* and any tests/, __tests__/, fixtures/ or __fixtures__/ dir. This includes certified-provider.json and vm-control.mjs.
- scripts/mods/: everything except *.test.ts and .claude-plugin/types/.
- docs/roles/: JetBrains ships the whole dir. VS Code ships only architect.md, qa.md and worker.md.
- docs/agent-context.md and docs/skills/.
Keep the build-from-source commands. A `cd moe-vscode && npm run package` line is optional; vscode:prepublish runs the bundler.

(b) GUARDS, one bullet each:
1. Required-asset lists that fail the build: JetBrains requireBundledAssets() (prepareSandbox doFirst) and the checks in bundle-assets.mjs. The build fails on a missing or stale (older than src) daemon/proxy dist, missing node_modules, or a missing local-runner certified-provider.json, multipass.mjs, doctor.mjs, cli.mjs or vm-control.mjs. Only JetBrains also requires moe-agent.ps1, moe-agent.sh and moe-call.sh; VS Code copies the other scripts only when they are present.
2. `node scripts/tests/onboarding.mjs <extracted bundle>` packaged checks:
   - the required helpers exist;
   - bundled vm-control.mjs run with no args exits 2 and prints {"code":"VM_CONTROL_INPUT_INVALID"}, so its whole import closure loads from the bundle;
   - no test artifact under daemon/, proxy/ or scripts/, skipping node_modules.
   The full onboarding flow then runs on the bundled daemon and proxy. CI runs it on the extracted JetBrains zip ('Verify packaged JetBrains onboarding'). release.yml also runs it on the extracted .vsix.
3. scripts/tests/local-runner-bundle.test.mjs runs the real VS Code bundler on a fixture and replays onboarding's packaged checks on that output. It also statically checks build.gradle.kts and ci.yml. CI runs it on ubuntu, windows and macos ('Test local runner prerequisite bundles').

(c) RECORD. Add '### Client verification record (CQ-I)' at the end of the section, before its `---`. Make it a short table with columns Contract | Proved by | Where it runs | Not certified, and these rows:
1. /ws CLIENT_HELLO and approval admission. Proved by daemon vitest src/server/WebSocketServer.test.ts ('capability negotiation v1') and src/server/planApproval.test.ts. Runs in CI test-typescript (ubuntu). Not certified: no IDE sends CLIENT_HELLO; there is no sender in moe-jetbrains/src/main or moe-vscode/src.
2. Shared verdict corpus (approval binding, reconnect, managed-VM decode). The corpus is moe-jetbrains/src/test/resources/client-verdicts.json, sections approval and vm. JUnit ClientVerdictCorpusTest reads it in CI build-plugin (ubuntu). node:test moe-vscode/tests/plan-review.test.cjs and managed-vm-verdicts.test.cjs read it in 'Test VS Code daemon startup' (3 OS).
3. Packaging: the three guards above.
4. Windows engines.
   - Both IDEs launch Windows seats with Windows PowerShell 5.1 (`powershell`): JetBrains util/TerminalAgentLauncher.kt powerShellLine, VS Code src/util/AgentLauncher.ts buildPowerShellCommand.
   - CI windows-latest runs the landing-guard and wrapper post-flight suites under Windows PowerShell 5.1 and PowerShell 7, onboarding on Windows Node, and the VS Code tests.
   - Not certified: JetBrains JUnit runs on ubuntu only.
5. Native provider smoke and isolation certification: `node scripts/local-runner/cli.mjs certify --work-dir <abs>`, plus `native-smoke --work-dir <abs>`, which is provider-support evidence only. Both are operator-invoked on real hardware, never in CI. For per-platform state, link [CERTIFICATION.md](CERTIFICATION.md#certified-platforms) and state no result.
6. Headless only. Every row runs headless (vitest, JUnit, node:test, Node scripts), and the Managed VMs tests use fakes. No IntelliJ sandbox (runIde) or VS Code Extension Host interaction is certified, and no test launches a real VM.
7. verified-local stays unavailable. The daemon refuses it with EXECUTION_PROFILE_NOT_READY (packages/moe-daemon/src/delivery/executionProfile.ts and its test). Neither IDE offers it:
   - both Managed VMs surfaces always show the strong profile as unavailable (ManagedVmPresentationTest, managed-vm.test.cjs);
   - VS Code settings never send executionProfile or deliveryPolicy (settings-wire.test.cjs S6).

RULES:
- No run counts, versions or dates; evidence belongs in complete_task. Engine names such as Windows PowerShell 5.1 and PowerShell 7 are identities, not evidence, and stay.
- Restate no per-platform certification state.
- Never write that the daemon never runs git (packages/moe-daemon/src/util/daemonGitDocs.test.ts scans this file).

planningNotes.codebaseInsights:
The two bundles differ in a few ways:
- JetBrains adds lib/ and ships all of docs/roles. VS Code ships only architect/qa/worker.md.
- Only JetBrains requires moe-agent.ps1/.sh and moe-call.sh. VS Code copies non-local-runner scripts only if they exist.
- Both require the same 5 local-runner files and refuse a stale dist.
- CI runs onboarding on the built JetBrains zip (build-plugin, ubuntu) and runs local-runner-bundle.test.mjs on 3 OS. release.yml alone runs onboarding on the extracted .vsix (extension/bundled).
- Daemon vitest runs on ubuntu only (test-typescript). JUnit runs on ubuntu only (build-plugin).
- Windows CI runs the landing guard and wrapper post-flight under both powershell and pwsh, plus VS Code npm test.
- No IDE sends CLIENT_HELLO.
- VM cleanup goes through holdReason, which turns an unreachable daemon into 'attempt-unknown' (kept). vm-control's Multipass is pinned per platform (platform-*.mjs EXECUTABLE).
